narr: A large area of high pressure centered over the southeast CONUS allowed for a warm, tropical airmass to advect northward into northern OH. Surface dewpoints in the low 70s and PWAT's near 2 provided a thermodynamically favorable environment for heavy rainfall. A west to east oriented cold front slowly drifted south through the Great Lakes towards the local area which, in concert with several residual outflow boundaries from thunderstorms during the night preceding the event, provided the focus for convective development. The heaviest rainfall occurred over Stark County, where thunderstorms developed and moved southeast through the county, dropping in excess of 1 to 2.5 of rainfall in just over one hour.
ev: Approximately 30 to 40 cars were flooded in the parking lot of Belden Village Mall in North Canton. A business and car at the intersection of Whipple Ave. and Portage St. was flooded. Flooding was reported in the southern part of Price Park due to Zimber Ditch flooding out of its banks. The USGS streamgage just downstream of the park reported a crest of 10.18 ft. at 1830 EST, after rising above the 9.5 ft. minor flood stage at approximately 1415 EST. Farther upstream near the headwaters of Zimber Ditch, a car dealership was flooded, with 6 to 12 inches of flowing water in the parking lot up to the doors of the showroom.
